Coursework, thesis and code, 2024–2026

Bachelor's thesis · in progress · 2026

AI-based energy demand forecasting to support renewable integration in the European iron and steel industry

Steel is one of Europe's most electricity-intensive industries, and better demand forecasts make it easier to plan around variable wind and solar supply. I run forecasting models on real European data and compare traditional statistical methods with AI-based methods.

Engineering Design · my part of a 4-person project · 2026

Car scissor jack: from calculation to printed prototype

Each of us designed one mechanism; the scissor jack was mine. I calculated the lifting mechanism, modelled its 10 components in SolidWorks, animated the assembly and 3D-printed the parts on a Prusa MK4S, my first print. The printed nut's thread wasn't accurate enough to run smoothly, so I corrected it by post-processing until the jack worked.

SolidWorksmotion studyPrusaSlicerPLAmechanism design

Industrial mixer: the mixing unit

Our team designed an industrial mixing machine. I modelled and drew the whole mixing unit: mixing rod, propeller, inlet and outlet rotors, screw and nut, with materials, tolerances and assembly drawings. Teammates drew the frame, motor arm and wheels.

Waste heat recovery with an organic Rankine cycle

Designed an ORC with cyclohexane as the working fluid: evaporation at 250 °C with 10 K superheat, condensing at 40 °C, with a recuperator. Plotted the cycle on the log p–h diagram and calculated the power output and efficiency.

Energy Systems · team of 5 · 2025

Microgrid design in HOMER Pro

Modelled a microgrid for a medium office in Houghton, USA: solar irradiance and load data, grid tariffs, then six energy sources (PV, a Tesla Powerpack battery, two generators, a converter and the grid) sized and compared on net present cost over 20 years at an 8% discount rate.
